text: Study Sources 1 and 2.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
‘We need to spend more money on healthcare locally.’
What are the strengths and weaknesses of the argument supporting this claim?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘People in this area are healthier than they were a year ago.’
How could you test this claim? You may consider the types of information, sources of evidence
or methods you might use.

text: Study Source 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify one opinion from Zama’s statement. Explain why this is an opinion.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why Sinta’s statement might be biased.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Which argument is more convincing, Zama’s or Sinta’s?
Your answer should consider both arguments and you should support your point of view with
their words.
You should also consider:
• the strength of their reasoning and evidence
• their use of language
• the different kinds of information used.

text: Study Source 4.
A government wants to improve the health of everyone in their country.
The following actions are being considered:
• Teach families about healthier lifestyles.
• Spend more money on healthcare and hospitals.
• Improve employment opportunities.
Which one of these suggestions would you recommend to the government and why?
In your answer, you should:
• state your recommendation
• give reasons and evidence to support your choice
• use the material in the sources and/or any of your own ideas
• consider different arguments and perspectives.
